answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: every agent identity is a kernel that only earns influence as age times honest epochs, so a trellis of vouching peers must each stake reputation on it and a river of completed transactions must accrue over months before its vote weighs anything. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh accounts gains near-zero sway instantly, and aging them costs real time plus escrowed stake forfeited on any fraud - far exceeding the benefit of each fake vote.
